title: Continuous coefficient rings and etale slice restrictions
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and a topological commutative ring $T$, let $T_X$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] have sections $C(|V|,T)$, pointwise operations, and restrictions by precomposition. For a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], give $E$ its spectral norm topology and its valuation ring $A$ the subspace topology. Set $E_X=(E)_X$, $A_X=(A)_X$, and let $A_X\to E_X$ be postcomposition with inclusion. For an etale arrow $f:Y\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], the functor $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ composes structure maps with $f$; its coefficient comparison $E_Y\to f_*E_X$ is identity on continuous functions.

lean.note: §1(B): the published continuous-function coefficient interface restricts its coefficient ring to Type 0, while the finite-monodromy and representation interfaces use the larger site universe u+1. This module supplies the identical pointwise continuous-function construction for coefficients in Type (u+1), on the unchanged site with objects in u+1 and morphisms in u. It imports and retains the small-coefficient API, uses the same spectral and subspace topologies, and constructs the inclusion and slice comparison by postcomposition and the identity. No universe equality is imposed.
